title: SDK embedding integration and operational playbook (Dedicated & Hosted)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a prescriptive integration and operational checklist for customers embedding Redwood Inference via SDKs (server-side embeddings, reranking, and generation) in Dedicated and Hosted modes. It covers prerequisites, step-by-step integration, production configuration recommendations, health checks and QBR telemetry, a tiered escalation matrix, common failure modes with workarounds, and a support bundle/rollback procedure. Use this doc during onboarding, handoff to SRE/Platform teams, and quarterly review preparation.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Server-side SDK integrations for embedding/embedding pipelines, reranking flows, and generation endpoints. Includes both Hosted API and Dedicated capacity deployments.
- Audience: Customer Success Manager (CSM), Solutions Engineers (SE), customer's Platform/SRE, Redwood Support on-call, and Account Engineering.

Owners and SLAs:
- Primary owner: Customer Success (Aisha Patel)
- SE technical owner: Marco Nguyen
- Support escalation owner: Redwood Critical Incidents (on-call)
- Onboarding SLA (internal): 7 business days from kickoff to working POC; 30 days to first production rollout for standard integrations.

Prerequisites (customer & Redwood):
- Customer provides: API key or mTLS cert, VPC peering details (for Private/Dedicated), expected QPS/throughput profile, representative dataset (10–1000 prompts), and success criteria.
- Redwood provides: Dedicated capacity config proposal (GPU type, slots), SDK package (versioned), network allowlist entries, example pipeline repo, and an initial perf baseline.

Integration checklist (recommended order):
1) Kickoff & access
   - Verify contact list and escalation contacts (section: Escalation matrix).
   - Exchange API keys / service account or configure mTLS certificate.
2) Environment validation
   - Confirm network egress/ingress rules: TLS 1.2+, allow outbound 443 to api.redwood.ai and dedicated endpoint IPs/subnets as provided.
   - Validate time sync (NTP) on customer hosts.
3) Install SDK and example app
   - Use pinned SDK: pip install redwood-sdk==1.8.0 (example).
   - Run minimal embedding example against sandbox and verify response (min payload and latency).
4) Performance profiling with representative traffic
   - Run 1k sample requests with sequence length distribution matching production. Capture latency P50/P95, CPU/GPU utilization, and token-per-second throughput.
   - If Dedicated: validate pool size handles peak concurrency with <150ms P95 for embeddings (target depends on GPU tier).
5) Configure batching and cache
   - Recommended batching window: 5–20ms for short requests; for throughput-sensitive workloads use 50–100ms and larger batch sizes.
   - Enable prefix/KV cache when request reuse >10% to reduce token cost.
6) Integrate observability hooks
   - Add per-request trace_id and propagate: X-Request-ID header.
   - Emit metrics: request_count, request_error_count, tokens_consumed, batch_size_distribution, kv_cache_hit_rate, backend_latency_ms.
   - Push traces to our instrumented collector or export OpenTelemetry spans to the customer APM.
7) Run acceptance tests and quality checks
   - Run a small eval set (100–500 prompts) and compare generation/embedding similarity baselines.
   - Record and save failing prompts for regression alerts.
8) Staged rollout and canary
   - Start 5% traffic canary for 24–72 hours, monitor SLOs, then 25%, then 100%. Use automatic rollback on error budget breach.

Production configuration recommendations:
- Timeouts: client request timeout = 30s; token stream timeouts vary by model.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter; idempotency keys for safe retries.
- Batching: dynamic batching enabled in SDK; tune max_batch_tokens and max_batch_size per model.
- Quantization: if customer requires lower cost, recommend int8 quantized variant with quality regression tests.
- Rate limiting: set a per-key rate limit and a circuit breaker threshold at 5xx rate > 1% in 5-minute window.

Network & security checklist:
- TLS requirement: all traffic must use TLS; mutual TLS available for Private/Dedicated.
- IP allowlist: provide dedicated CIDR range for Dedicated deployments.
- KMS/HSM: for Private deployments, integrate keys via the customer KMS; confirm rotation cadence.
- Audit logs: enable request/response logging at 90-day retention for compliance customers (obfuscate PII per policy).

Observability, SLOs, and QBR telemetry:
- Recommended SLOs (example):
  - Availability: 99.95% (prod) measured as HTTP 2xx fraction per month.
  - Latency: Generation P95 < 500ms (small models) / < 1200ms (long-context models); Embedding P95 < 200ms.
  - Error rate: HTTP 5xx < 0.1% monthly, request timeouts < 0.5%.
- Daily/weekly dashboards:
  - Token consumption and cost by route/model, per-customer.
  - Latency distribution P50/P95/P99 and tail latencies by model and time window.
  - KV cache hit rate and batching efficiency.
  - Regression alerts: prompt-set accuracy drift over time.
- QBR metrics to report to customer: average monthly spend, 30/90/365 day latency trends, top 10 error classes, active prompts failing QA, planned infra changes.

Health checks and automated probes (examples):
1) SDK probe (every 60s): call /v1/health with minimal payload to verify auth and basic model response. Return codes: 200 OK => healthy; 429 => rate limited; 5xx => backend failure.
2) Latency probe (every 30s): send representative short request and measure P95 across 5 probes. Alert if P95 > configured threshold for 5-minute window.
3) KV cache probe (every 5m): prewarm and then measure cache hit for repeated request.

Severity & escalation matrix:
- Sev 1 (Critical): Production-wide outage or sustained SLO breach impacting >20% customers (or customer-critical path).
  - Response goals: acknowledge < 15 min, initial workaround in 30–60 min, continuous updates every 30 min.
  - Primary action: page on-call infra, notify CSM and SE, open incident ticket in PagerDuty and Incident Board.
- Sev 2 (High): Degraded performance for a single customer or partial capacity degradation.
  - Response goals: acknowledge < 1 hour, mitigation in 4 hours, updates every 2 hours.
  - Primary action: SE investigates tuning and config; consider temporary capacity increase or canary rollback.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Functional bug with workaround available; non-urgent customer impact.
  - Response goals: acknowledge < 24 hours, fix planned in next sprint or hotfix.
  - Primary action: Support creates JIRA, assigns to engineering backlog as appropriate.

Escalation path (contacts and steps):
1) Support Tier 1 (Customer Success/Support) – triage and gather support bundle.
2) Support Tier 2 (Solutions Engineering) – reproduce, check Dedicated pool health, batching, and cache.
3) On-call Runtime/Infra – kernel/runtime, GPU health, autoscaler.
4) Incident Commander (if Sev1) – coordinate cross-functional war room.

Contact template (use in every escalation ticket):
- Customer name, account id, contact mobile/email, environment (Hosted/Dedicated), observed impact, first seen timestamp (UTC), steps to reproduce, support bundle link, SLA target.

Support bundle (what to collect before Tier 2 handoff):
- Sample failing requests (max 100) and their timestamps.
- SDK version and client logs (including X-Request-IDs).
- Server-side metrics: GPU utilization, per-host CPU/memory, network egress, batch sizes, cache hit rates for the incident window.
- Topology: dedicated pool size and instance types, autoscaling events, recent deployments, rollback history.
- Logs: application + nginx/ingress + runtime logs (last 48 hours).
- Trace spans for 5 failed requests.

Common failure modes and mitigations (observed patterns):
- Symptom: sudden spike in 5xx errors after deployment.
  - Likely causes: model hot reload bug, kernel incompatibility, or bad quantized weights.
  - Mitigation: roll back to previous model version, disable new kernels, escalate to runtime team.
- Symptom: slow tail latencies for embeddings at peak.
  - Likely causes: insufficient batching, cold KV cache, noisy neighbors in Dedicated pool.
  - Mitigation: increase batching window, prewarm cache, scale pool or isolate workloads.
- Symptom: elevated token cost with low quality improvements.
  - Likely causes: model mismatch or prompt inflation.
  - Mitigation: A/B test smaller model or quantized variant; tighten prompt templates.

Rollback & remediation playbook (when to roll back):
- Criteria to rollback: error rate > 2% sustained for 15 minutes, latency P95 > 2x baseline for 10 min, or semantic regressions on saved prompt set.
- Rollback steps:
  1) Announce rollback to stakeholders and pause deployments.
  2) Trigger model/server rollback via Redwood Console (canary abort) or runbook script.
  3) Validate health probes and key metrics for 15 minutes.
  4) Reopen deployment only after stability confirmed or open a postmortem and mitigation plan.

Post-incident triage and QBR prep:
- After any Sev1/2 incident: run RCA within 72 hours, publish postmortem linked to the incident board, attach support bundle, and assign action items with owners and due dates.
- QBR prep checklist: gather monthly metrics, incident summary, cost optimization recommendations, and roadmap items affecting the customer.

Appendix: examples and snippets
- Minimal embedding request (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"input": "Redwood inference test prompt"}'

- Example SDK config (yaml):
  sdk:
    version: "1.8.0"
    batching:
      enabled: true
      max_batch_size: 64
      max_delay_ms: 25
    retries:
      max_attempts: 3
      backoff_ms: 200
    observability:
      enable_traces: true
      metrics_endpoint: "otlp://collector.local:4317"

- Quick support bundle collection (bash):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  mkdir -p /tmp/support_bundle
  cp /var/log/redwood/*.log /tmp/support_bundle/ || true
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/metrics?since=48h" -o /tmp/support_bundle/metrics.json
  tar czf /tmp/support_bundle_$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz -C /tmp support_bundle

Change log (brief):
- 2025-11-10: Initial draft and internal review.
- 2026-01-12: Added KV cache probes and updated SLO targets for embeddings.
- 2026-02-18: Clarified escalation timeboxes and included support bundle script.

Notes and references:
- See related onboarding templates and the enterprise support lifecycle playbook for Dedicated-specific contract clauses.
- For Private deployments, confirm KMS integration and audit retention settings before enabling debug-level logging.

This playbook is intended to be a living document; please send suggestions and updates to the owner (Aisha Patel) or propose edits via the Confluence page comments.
